first_in_archive: Take Me Out to the Ballgame Tuning

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (2 reviews, 1 other source): This is the first show starting with China Cat Sunflower, jamming into I Know You Rider; Transition from China Cat Sunflower sounds like heading into Greatest Story, which didn't exist yet [1][2][9]
- **Alligator** (1 review): Alligator sounds especially slow due to speed issues in the recording [3]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The Other One is a mind blower, serving as a great end to the set [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **I Know You Rider**: back after 137 archived shows (787 days) [14]
- **Merry-Go-Round Broke down**: rare: 7 archived performances [14]
- **Take Me Out to the Ballgame Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]

## The recordings

- **gd69-09-30.aud.early.hollister.80.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 7 songs; 34 min; rated 3.25/5 by 12 [1]. Said about its sound: Vocals are barely audible, requiring significant effort to listen to the recording; Speed problems, hiss, and muddiness reduce the appeal of the performance; The recording is a hoot to listen to, requiring active ear use and EQ [2][3][4][5][6][7][8][12]

## Around the show

- The presence of the first China to Rider transition is historically interesting [3]
- Band caught the Baseball Fever gripping NYC as the Miracle Mets overtook the Cubs [8]
- The previous night's show at Cafe au Go-Go has some phenomenal jams [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-09-30.aud.early.hollister.80.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience [1]. Also: AUD transferred to cassette twice, then XLR into SV-3700, ZA2, SoundForge, CD [1]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Worthpoint: [Original Grateful Dead Poster Cafe au Go Go June 1966 | #41288747](https://www.worthpoint.com/worthopedia/original-grateful-dead-poster-cafe-au-go-go-june) [15]
